newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner backs Sjoinvest hopes for Western Bulk.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner backs Sjoinvest hopes for Western Bulk.

text.p: Kvaerner ASA, the Norwegian engineering group, said on Tuesday it supported Sjoinvest's hopes to develop bulk shipping firm Western Bulk Shipping.

Kvaerner also confirmed it would not sell its 18 percent stake in Western Bulk at the price currently on offer from Belships Company Ltd Ships-ASA, Sjoinvest's rival for control of the handymax bulk ship operator.
Kvaerner spokesman Trond Andresen said: "We see that Sjoinvest has complete focus on Western Bulk, and we think that could be good for that company, as well as our shareholding in it."

However, he added that Kvaerner had not yet undertaken any detailed discussions with Sjoinvest about its plans for the firm, nor had Kvaerner yet taken any decision to support any new directors proposed by Sjoinvest.
"We have observed that they have called a shareholders meeting, but we have not taken any decision on that yet," Andresen said.

Sjoinvest, a private Norwegian shipping investment firm, called earlier Tuesday for an extraordinary general meeting of Western Bulk shareholders at which it intends to propose an undisclosed number of new directors.

Belships hopes to gain majority control of Western Bulk, to cement historic ties between the two firms. Belships offer of 38 Norwegian crowns per Western Bulk share will not be accepted, the Kvaerner spokesman said.

"What we can see is that the offer is at 38 crowns per share, while they are trading today at 40 crowns," Andresen said. "That shows we are not alone in our thinking that these shares are worth more." The offer values Western Bulk at 517 million crowns.

Andresen confirmed Kvaerner's Western Bulk stake was a candidate for disposal, although there was no urgency for a quick sale. "We believe Western Bulk has quite a lot of potential, which we believe Sjoinvest has shown the most interest in releasing," he said. -- Reuters Shipping News +44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 5017
